issues.description: OutputImageRawFrame is constructed with format='RGB' but image.tobytes() reflects PIL's actual mode, which may be RGBA/P/L for PNG/WebP outputs
issues.detail: PIL's Image.open on bytes from Gemini does not guarantee an RGB mode; many model outputs decode as RGBA (PNG with alpha) or palette modes. The code calls image.tobytes() without converting (e.g., image.convert('RGB')), so the raw byte buffer's pixel layout will not match the declared format='RGB'. Downstream consumers expecting 3 bytes/pixel will either render garbled frames, crash on size mismatch (W*H*3 vs W*H*4), or silently produce wrong colors. This is a correctness bug at the data-structure boundary: the invariant 'bytes length == width*height*3' is not established. Fix by image = image.convert('RGB') before tobytes(), or by passing the actual mode through.

issues.description: Mutating a private module attribute genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE at import time is a fragile global hack with unstated invariant
issues.detail: The comment self-labels this as a 'Temporary hack', but the mutation is performed unconditionally at module import and reaches into a leading-underscore submodule of a third-party library. The invariant being established ('5 MiB is large enough for any Nano Banana image') is asserted, not justified, and the constant will silently rot when google-genai refactors _api_client or removes the attribute. At minimum this needs (a) a guard (hasattr check) so import does not break on future versions, (b) a justification of why 5 MiB is the right bound, and (c) a tracking issue referenced in the comment so the hack can be removed when upstream supports configuration.

issues.description: Image-generation branch has no loop/termination reasoning when multiple inline_data parts arrive in a single candidate
issues.detail: The new elif simply pushes a frame per part with inline_data, but there is no stated invariant about ordering of text parts vs. image parts within a candidate, nor about how OutputImageRawFrame interleaves with LLMTextFrame emissions earlier in the same loop. For a streaming pipeline this matters: a reader of this code cannot tell whether the contract is 'one image per response', 'images may be interleaved with text tokens', or 'images always trail text'. A one-line literate comment stating the contract (and a check that part.inline_data.mime_type starts with 'image/' rather than trusting any inline_data) would make the code auditable.

issues.description: Default model change from gemini-2.0-flash to gemini-2.5-flash is a silent behavior change for every existing caller
issues.detail: Changing a default in a service constructor is a semantic version event: every user who relied on the previous default now gets a different model with different latency, cost, token accounting, and thinking-budget behavior (the new _maybe_unset_thinking_budget logic is gated on 'gemini-2.5-flash'). The CHANGELOG notes it under 'Changed' but the code carries no deprecation path or warning. The invariant 'callers who did not pass model get stable behavior across minor versions' is being broken; either keep the old default and document the new recommended value, or emit a one-time logger.warning when the default is taken.

Substring matching for 'image' is too loose and too tight at once: it will match any future model whose name happens to contain 'image' (including unrelated ones), and it does not document the invariant that image-generation Gemini models do not accept a thinking_config. A more precise predicate (explicit allowlist of image-capable model names, or a check against a documented capability flag) would be both more readable and more defensible to a reader trying to understand why this branch exists.

issues.description: PIL Image and io are used in the new branch but the diff does not show their imports being added in this hunk
issues.detail: The new code calls Image.open(io.BytesIO(...)) but the visible diff does not introduce the imports. If they are already present in the module this is fine, but a reviewer cannot confirm the invariant 'all referenced names resolve' from the diff alone. Worth a sanity check; if missing, import-time NameError will occur only when an image part is received, which is a latent failure mode that tests against text-only models will not catch.

issues.description: Dependency upper bound widened from ~=1.24.0 to >=1.41.0,<2 invites silent breakage
issues.detail: Moving from a compatible-release (~=1.24.0) constraint to a half-open <2 range is a deliberate trade of stability for flexibility. That is a legitimate choice, but the diff does not record the test matrix that justifies it. Since this same module monkey-patches genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE, any minor release of google-genai inside [1.41, 2) can quietly remove that attribute. The two changes together amplify each other's risk; pinning a tighter upper bound until the buffer-size hack is removed would be the conservative move.

review.summary: The PR is a small, mostly clean feature addition, but it has one P0 correctness issue at the image-decoding boundary: image.tobytes() with a hard-coded format='RGB' does not honor the actual PIL mode of the decoded bytes, so RGBA/palette outputs will produce frames whose byte length disagrees with width*height*3. The genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE monkey-patch is self-described as a hack and should at minimum be guarded, justified, and tracked, especially given the simultaneous widening of the google-genai version range. The default-model change is reasonable but is a silent behavior shift for every existing caller and deserves a deprecation note or runtime warning. Decision: UNDER-AUDITED — the algorithm is small and probably correct in the happy path, but invariants around image format, part ordering, and third-party private-attribute access are not stated and the analysis is missing.
